cards.text: Paul is writing a letter to the believers in Galatia, and he's just told them each one is a son now, and an heir through God. But friend, this next part gets PERSONAL. He takes them back to the days before they knew God.

cards.question: Before they knew God, the Galatians were ___ to those who by nature are not gods.

cards.text: But now they know God, or rather, Paul says, they are known by God. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer where everybody forgot I was there, so trust me, being known is a BIG deal.

cards.question: Now that the Galatians know God, what does Paul say they're doing?

answers.text: Going back to weak and worthless principles
Chasing after rich and powerful friends
Arguing over small and petty disputes

cards.question: Paul asks the Galatians if they want to be enslaved by those weak and worthless principles all over again.

cards.text: Then Paul names what they're actually doing: observing special days and months and seasons and years. He's not guessing, friend. He's got receipts.

cards.question: Right after naming those special days and seasons, Paul tells the Galatians that he ___ for them.
Paul fears that his efforts for the Galatians may have been in vain.

cards.text: Then Paul pleads with them: "I beg you, brothers, become like me, for I became like you."

cards.question: Paul tells the Galatians they have done him wrong.

cards.text: Then Paul takes them back to the first time he preached the gospel to them. Spoiler, friend: it was NOT his best day.

cards.question: Paul reminds the Galatians why he first preached the gospel to them. What was the reason?

cards.text: Paul's illness was a trial to them. Most folks see a sick guest coming up the walk and suddenly remember they left the oven on, but the Galatians didn't despise him or reject him.

cards.question: Paul was sick when he came, but the Galatians didn't reject him. How did they welcome him?

answers.text: As if he were an angel of God
As if he were a king of Israel
As if he were a long lost brother

cards.question: Paul says the Galatians welcomed him as if he were Christ Jesus Himself.

cards.text: Paul is still thinking about how the Galatians first welcomed him, and now he asks them, "What then has become of your blessing?" He remembers what they would have handed over for him back then.

cards.question: What does Paul say the Galatians would have given him back then?

cards.text: Their own EYES, friend, and I know folks who won't even give up their parking spot for me! Then Paul asks the Galatians a hard question.

cards.question: Paul asks if he has now become the Galatians' ___ by telling them the truth.

cards.text: Then Paul talks about some other people, the ones he said earlier were troubling the Galatians and trying to distort the gospel of Christ (Galatians 1:7). He says those people are zealous for the Galatians, but not in a good way.

cards.question: Paul says those people aren't zealous for the Galatians in a good way. What does he say they want to do to the Galatians?

answers.text: Isolate them from Paul and those with him
Take their money and their homes from them
Hand them over to the local rulers

cards.question: Paul says those people want the Galatians to be zealous for them.

cards.text: You know the type: the coworker who's suddenly your BEST friend, but only if you leave your old group chat and join theirs. Then Paul has something to say about being zealous itself.

cards.question: Paul tells the Galatians that being zealous is never a good thing.
Paul says it's good to be zealous if it serves a noble purpose. When does he say that should happen?

answers.text: At any time and not just when he's with them
Only when he is there with them in person
Only when they meet together to pray

cards.text: Then Paul calls the Galatians his children. And he says he's going through something for them all over again.

cards.question: Paul calls the Galatians his children and says he is again in the pains of ___ for them.
Paul says he'll be in those pains for the Galatians until Christ is formed in them.

cards.text: Then Paul says he wishes he could be with the Galatians right now. Friend, I can't leave a batch in the oven without hovering over it, and Paul is a whole letter away from his people!

cards.question: Paul says he wishes he could be with the Galatians right now. What would he change?

cards.text: Why? Because, he says, he's perplexed about them. But he still calls them his children, and I bet he hasn't stopped hoping.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the observation of special days, "He's not guessing, friend," and "He's got receipts." Combine the wording so the card stays within two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: "Why?", the statement about Paul being perplexed, and the closing statement about his children and hope. Rewrite it as one or two sentences.
